BiblicalUsage: The oak, the strong tree, and the prophets use it to measure what is left. In Isaiah, when the land is desolate and the tenth is burned, yet the stock remains like a teil tree and as an oak, whose substance is in them when they cast their leaves. And Zechariah cries, Howl, O ye oaks of Bashan, for the forest of the vintage is come down.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for an oak carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the stump in Isaiah, that even when the tree is cut down the substance is still in it, and God can grow it again.
